question: How many entries does this memory hold, and which lines do not parse?
why: Found on the day this catalogue was created. src/doctor.mjs walked every drawer itself and counted its own unparsable lines - four hundred lines below checkIntegrity, which calls scanIntegrity for the very same walk. Two calculations of one question, in one file. The hand-rolled one was also worse advice: scanIntegrity knows the file and line of every broken entry, while the copy could only offer a grep recipe.

question: When are two entry bodies the same text?
why: Entered the day src/inbox.mjs needed body equality for replay-vs-conflict. The tempting shortcut was `a === b`, which would have called a retry differing only in line endings a CONFLICT and lost a message. Normalisation has many defensible variants (whitespace, case, CRLF, unicode); two of them in one house means two answers to 'is this the same text', and the one you believe is a coin toss.

question: How far has this memory come, so that a rollback is detectable?
why: Entered preventively. The watermark only works if exactly one recipe computes it: a second version hashing the same ids in a different order, or over a different set, would disagree with the stored mark and report a rollback that never happened. A rollback alarm that cries wolf gets switched off, and then the real rollback passes unnoticed.

question: Which drawers exist in this memory?
why: DISCARDED on the day of entry, after counting. 35 places use this idiom, and almost all of them ask something else entirely - a CLI help line listing the known types, an MCP schema enum, a dedupe command defaulting to all types. integrity.logFiles is genuinely the owner of 'which logs exist' and is already called from epoch.mjs, state.mjs and doctor.mjs; the one real second walker was fixed the same day. A latch that reports 34 innocents gets switched off, and then it stops catching the guilty too. Worth revisiting if a second enumeration ever produces a wrong number.

question: Is a duty fresh, due or overdue - and which field carries its due date?
why: Before the due-date core (build plan Q1) today.mjs and dashboard-data.mjs read 'due ?? by' and appointment-today.mjs looped over due / due_date / until / deadline - three readers, a handful of guessed names, and the sibling house's four readers guessed five. Now only src/due.mjs reads the field name (dueValue, dueText) and decides the state; every other reader asks there. The pattern has four branches. (1) Any property read named due / due_date / until / deadline (x.due, x?.deadline) or the alias name due_date; deliberately wide, because a duty's variable can be called anything. (2) A destructuring that pulls one of the four names out of an object (`const { due } = d`, `{ due: x } = d`, `for (const { due } of rows)`, `({ due }) =>`, with quoted keys and defaults); an object LITERAL such as `{ due: x }` is not matched, only a pattern that is assigned to, iterated or taken as a parameter. (3) A bracket access with a literal name (`d["due"]`, `d['deadline']`, a template key). (4) The alias fallback idiom `due ?? by` / `deadline || x.by`. A bare `.by` cannot be searched for: `by` is also the author field of claims, appointments and deletions, so only a read chained after one of the four names counts; the core itself is the only duty reader of `by` (dueValue, ALIASES). Since the sharpening the core no longer hands out results under the raw field's name, so a destructuring of a core result is not mistaken for a read of a duty: situationFromOpen returns the count of the state as `dueNow` and the text of a row as `dueAt` (the CLI and bridge JSON keep the public key `due` through rowForOutput), and the day list of appointment-today is `dueList`. The price is the files in `except`, which use the SAME words for other things - a claim's `until` (claim.mjs, agents, mem-mcp claim lines), a silence's `until` (appointments, dashboard), a login lock, a mail permit, the digest `due` check (board, doctor, search), a cache's `until` (dashboard-data, mcplive), an invite token's `until`, a time window `{ since, until }` (questiontext.mjs: an options parameter of the question read, no duty), and today.mjs, which renders the rows of the deadline and decision parts (`{ state, due: value }` is the part's own passed-on text, already a string, and the dashboard reads the same key; today.mjs reads no duty). Files that read DUTIES themselves (appointment-today, write) are NOT excepted. bin/mem-mcp, dashboard-data, doctor and today.mjs are excepted for their other-domain or part-row hits and are the places to review by hand when a duty reader is added there.
